agree.reason: Long-tenured staff who don't want phone work get clear dates, first pick of shifts by seniority, and severance terms, but nothing makes the switch feel low-risk (the 6-month opt-out with severance is left out), so many will still start looking elsewhere.

honest.reason: It drops the unsupported 'better for everyone' claim and states the hard parts plainly, but it adds things the brief doesn't support: an unscheduled promise ('we're still working out how often each person will work until 8') and a mild implication that the branch jobs were insecure.

works_the_facts.reason: It writes 'same pay or higher' when the true figure is a stronger $1.50 an hour more, it never works the severance into an example (10 years = 20 weeks of pay), and it never turns the 9-minute hold time or the 60% rise into anything concrete.

right_comparison.reason: It sets the 44% fall in branch visits against the 60% rise in phone and chat contacts, which fairly frames the alternative of staying put, but it never sets the new role and the severance side by side in concrete terms.

qualification.reason: The offer and decision dates are concrete and checkable, but the open question about late shifts has no date and no consequence attached.

objections.reason: Seniority shift choice and work-from-home help, but the main objection (not wanting phone work) gets only '90 days of training'; the 6-month severance opt-out, the center's location and commute, the two weeks of rumours, and the phone team's 30% turnover are all left out.

fit.reason: It is an email from the COO of about 400 words with a clear subject and sections, though it leaves '[Your name]' as a placeholder when the name was known.
